title: Congress removes President Peña in impeachment after Ueno Bank crisis
detail: BBC News Mundo reports that Paraguay's Congress removed President Santiago Peña through impeachment (juicio político) following the Ueno Bank crisis. The opposition accuses Peña of conflict of interest over his ties to Grupo Vázquez, the conglomerate that owns Ueno Bank; other reports say he remained a business partner of the group until March 2025, while the bank says he was never a shareholder or investor. Paraguay's central bank seized and dissolved the digital lender in early November, freezing savings for millions of customers. An impeachment request against Peña and Vice President Pedro Alliana was filed on 4 November. The feed that triggered this tracker also claimed Peña was arrested; no source reviewed confirms an arrest, so that remains unverified.

title: Ousted president Peña transferred urgently to a regiment, testifies at prosecutor's office
detail: Clarín's live coverage of the Paraguay crisis reports that ousted president Santiago Peña was urgently transferred to a regiment and is due to testify at the prosecutor's office (Fiscalía) on 7 November. Only the headline was available to this update; the reason for the transfer and the subject of the testimony are not confirmed here.

title: Guarantees judge orders pretrial detention for ousted president Peña
detail: Judge Humberto Otazú ordered pretrial detention for Santiago Peña in the Ueno Bank investigation; prosecutors allege breach of trust and self-dealing administration. AFP reports custody at the Presidential Escort Regiment in Asunción. Pedro Alliana was sworn in to finish the term to August 2028. Prosecutors also sought detention for ex-central bank chief Carlos Carvallo. This clarifies the 8 Nov house-arrest vs. detention discrepancy: multiple outlets report pretrial detention.
